dominant_failure_factor: The ordered sweep, reclaim, opposite displacement, structure break, FVG and retrace sequence often identified a short local rotation, but it did not establish continued delivery to the opposite eight-hour external liquidity boundary. Removing sweep-flow alignment increased occurrence across all cycles without producing a single profitable trade.
invalid_generalizations: A failed external sweep plus CHoCH/BOS and FVG does not by itself imply full dealing-range traversal.
Aggressive flow aligned with the sweep is neither a sufficient continuation discriminator nor the main cause of the failure.
A very large geometric target-derived reward-risk ratio is not evidence that the target is probable.
valid_components: Frozen external-liquidity boundaries prevented hindsight movement of the dealing range.
The ordered state machine separated sweep detection from trade authorization.
Three of five ablation trades produced more than 1.5R favorable excursion before eventual failure, indicating useful local reaction timing.
Cycle component diagnostics showed the failure was not monopolized by one UTC session.
Current-NAV 3% risk sizing stayed within the planned loss budget under NautilusTrader execution.
next_design_implication: A successor may retain external sweep, reclaim and displacement as a local reaction detector, but must separately prove post-retrace acceptance and continuation before targeting distant external liquidity. Local reaction and range traversal are distinct states.
